title: "Race Conditions vs Data Races"

# Race Conditions vs Data Races

## Overview

These terms are not interchangeable. **Data races** are unsynchronized memory access (undefined, `-race` detects). **Race conditions** are logic timing bugs that can exist **without** a data race (atomics used wrong, check-then-act).

## Diagram

```text
  concurrent bug
     ├── data race      → memory model / -race
     └── race condition → wrong logic timing
                           (can be -race clean!)
```

## Data race example

```go
// two Gs: x++ without sync → data race
```

## Race condition without data race

```go
// Load, sleep, Add based on Load — atomic ops, still TOCTOU
if counter.Load()%2 == 0 {
	counter.Add(1)
} else {
	counter.Add(2)
}
```

## Check-then-act

```text
if !exists { create() }   // two Gs both pass check
```

Fix with mutex, single-flight, CAS loops, or DB uniqueness.

## Teaching rule

```text
-race clean ⇏ correct concurrent algorithm
correct algorithm ⇒ define happens-before for shared memory
```

## Experiment

Run the atomic composition examples from [259 atomics](259-atomics-complete.qmd) under `-race` (clean) and print varying totals (condition).

**Try next:** Find a production `if err := find(); err == notFound { insert }` and document the uniqueness constraint.
